keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Estonians. 'By the 13th century, eight major counties had developed' (Saaremaa, Läänemaa, Harjumaa, Rävala, Virumaa, Järvamaa, Sakala, Ugandi), each led by an elder; the Estonian Crusade page adds seven smaller counties. The page gives no area; the shape is the modern country of Estonia. 1208 is the year the crusaders began operations against the Estonians, the first year a page dates, not a founding.

Rotalia (Läänemaa) and Saaremaa remain until 1227: the page does not date Rotalia's fall (the Swedes lost at Lihula in 1220), so it is held to 1227 (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 1208: the crusaders open operations against the Estonians. 'By 1208 the Crusaders were strong enough to begin operations against the Estonians', raiding Sakala and Ugaunia with Liv and Latgalian allies. The counties are older; the Estonians 'were unable to develop their system of loose alliances into a centralised state', so no founding is dated.

1216: the Order invades Saaremaa. 'Danish landings failed in 1206 and 1222, and the Order invaded in 1216.'

ledger.note: August 1224: Tartu falls and the south is lost. 'Tharbata was finally captured by the crusaders in August 1224 and all its defenders were killed'; the Brothers set up headquarters at Fellin in 1224. The Bishopric of Dorpat shared the conquest (History of Estonia page).

ledger.note: 1227: Saaremaa falls and the last Estonian lands with it. 'Saaremaa fell after the Muhu and Valjala operations, and the Oeselians formally accepted Christianity'; 'The Sword Brethren conquered the last indigenous stronghold, on Saaremaa' (History of Estonia). Rotalia is held to 1227 in the same event (confidence 1 for Läänemaa).

ledger.note: 1227: the last free Estonian land is conquered; the ecclesiastical state Terra Mariana is established and the territory is divided among the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order, the Bishopric of Dorpat and the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, while the north stays a nominal Danish possession until 1346.

wars.outcome: The Estonians lost northern Estonia to the Danes (1219-1220), Sakala and Ugaunia to the Brothers of the Sword and the Bishop of Dorpat (Tartu, August 1224) and Saaremaa in 1227; the Treaty of Stensby of 7 June 1238 returned the Duchy of Estonia to Valdemar II.
wars.note: The St. Matthew's Day battle near Viljandi (21 September 1217) killed Lembitu, the elder of Sakala. The 1223 uprising retook all strongholds save Tallinn. William of Modena mediated a peace at Tarwanpe in 1226.

certainty.note: Counties without boundaries; the page names eight major and seven smaller counties and locates only Saaremaa, Harjumaa and Rävala. The shape is the modern country of Estonia, which includes areas of Livs and Latgalians and omits Estonians in northern Latvia.

notes: Not a state: the counties 'were unable to develop their system of loose alliances into a centralised state' (Estonian Crusade page); no capital, hence capitals is empty. Start 1208 is the first year a page dates events (the crusaders' first operations), not a founding; Estonians lived on the land long before, and the neutral map before 1208 is a data gap. The 'Ancient Estonia' Wikipedia page covers prehistory (8000 BC to the 13th century) with no county details; it was opened and not used (the History of Estonia page replaced it). Three pages used; Ancient Estonia was a fourth opened page that carried nothing. Not settled: the order of conquest of the counties (the page names only Sakala, Ugaunia, Revelia, Harrien, Vironia, Rotalia and Wiek), when Järvamaa and Läänemaa fell, Pärnu (Soontagana). The Livonian Brothers of the Sword dossier carries a contest with 'Estonians of Sakala and Ugandi' 1211-1227 and a Fellin gain in 1211; this dossier has the Estonians keep the south until August 1224, which conflicts with its 1218 southern-Estonia gain. The Livs and Latgalians in the Brothers' early lands have no dossier here (Livs: not written in this run).
